MG11.analysis: Goal: cook food without charcoal. Standard: burn fuel. Bottleneck: no fuel (bread fails). Violated assumption: heat must come from a fire. Reframe: foil is a reflector, umbrella a dish; the sun is the heat source. Solar cooker beats burning bread and is feasible.
MG11.final:
Step1: Line the inside of the open umbrella with the foil (shiny side up), forming a parabolic reflector.
Step2: Point it at the sun and put the food, wrapped in foil or in a beer can, at the focal point (wedge it on a stick or the umbrella shaft) to cook.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG12.analysis: Goal: tighten the loose screw. Standard: screwdriver. Bottleneck: no driver. Reframe: a thin flat edge can turn a slotted screw. The bent ruler's edge works as a flat blade; the stick can shim a stripped hole.
MG12.final:
Step1: Insert the thin end or corner of the metal ruler into the screw slot and turn clockwise until tight.
Step2: If it spins freely, jam a sliver of the popsicle stick into the hole, then re-tighten.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG13.analysis: Goal: stop torrential leak. Standard: patch plus sealant. Bottleneck: slow resin, wet cloth falls off. Reframe: a mechanical clamp is needed to hold the patch during cure, and dry heat speeds the cure. The inflated float can press the patch; the hairdryer dries and speeds curing.
MG13.final:
Step1: Dry the area with the hairdryer and roughen the metal around the hole with the file.
Step2: Soak the cloth in epoxy and press it over the hole from the inside.
Step3: Inflate the pool float and wedge it between the patch and the floor or a ladder to hold it firmly; warm with the hairdryer until cured.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG14.analysis: Goal: move snow into the pool. Standard: shovel or bucket. Bottleneck: tools leak. Reframe: need a non-porous carrier; the large blanket can hold and drag snow like a sled or tarp.
MG14.final:
Step1: Spread the blanket on the snow, wear the gloves, and pile snow onto it with your hands (spatula/dustpan to help).
Step2: Drag the blanket to the pool, lift the edges, and tip the snow in. Repeat.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG15.analysis: Goal: keep rain off the grill while cooking. Standard: lid or cover. Bottleneck: baking sheet too small. Reframe: build a composite cover. The sheet covers the central part, foil extends it and is waterproof, clothespins join pieces.
MG15.final:
Step1: Lay the baking sheet over the main cooking area.
Step2: Overlap and fold foil sheets to extend the cover over the remaining grill, joining seams by folding and clipping with the clothespins.
Step3: Drape the tablecloth over the foil for extra shield, leaving a gap for ventilation; use tongs to tend food.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG16.analysis: Goal: cover the saucepan. Standard: matching lid. Bottleneck: tray and board are oversized. A cover only needs to sit on the rim and be roughly round and flat. The thick round pizza stone fits that and holds heat.
MG16.final:
Step1: Place the thick round pizza stone on the saucepan rim as the lid (use the spoon or oven mitt to handle it when hot).
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG17.analysis: Goal: carry fish back. Standard: bucket or bag. Bottleneck: bag has holes, other items too small. Reframe: towels can plug the bag's holes, making a liner.
MG17.final:
Step1: Wrap the fish in a wet towel.
Step2: Place the wrapped fish inside the beach bag (the towel blocks the holes) and carry it.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG18.analysis: Goal: reach the mic to adjust it. Standard: stand on a stool. Bottleneck: books add little height, rod cannot attach. Reframe: only the chair is needed for height; books just supplement.
MG18.final:
Step1: Place the chair under the microphone and stand on it (stack books on the seat for extra height if stable).
Step2: Adjust the microphone by hand.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG19.analysis: Goal: obtain drinkable water. Standard: solar still with a sealed plastic sheet. Bottleneck: bag has holes. Reframe: fold the bag in layers so holes misalign, or collect dew on a cold smooth surface overnight. Feasible though low yield.
MG19.final:
Step1: At night, lay the sleeping mat (and the folded bag) flat and open to the air so dew condenses on them.
Step2: At dawn, wipe or shake the dew into the cup and drink.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG20.analysis: Goal: stop the mirror swiveling. Standard: tighten the mounting nut with a wrench. Bottleneck: wrench too big, tape not sticky. Reframe: add friction by wedging a thin spacer into the joint.
MG20.final:
Step1: Push the toothpick into the gap of the mirror pivot joint to wedge it tight.
Step2: Cut it flush with the knife.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE
